title: Protective Scheme Restoration Over a Completed Lower Shell Repair
abstract: Restoration of the protective scheme over a completed metallic repair in the lower shell, covering the chromate-free system, the bonding land exclusions and the inspection that closes the repair out.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the protective scheme over a completed metallic repair in the lower shell so that the repaired area has the same corrosion protection as the surrounding structure.
sections.damage_assessment: This scheme is applied after the structural repair is complete and accepted; it does not itself restore strength. Before it is applied, confirm that the repair record is closed, that no fastener is left to be installed and that no sealant fillet in the area is still uncured. Where the repair crosses a bonding land, record the position of every land before masking, because once the primer is on, the land is not visible and a bridged land will not be found until the next bonding check. Where the surrounding scheme is the older chromated system, the boundary must be feathered rather than butted, otherwise the step becomes a water trap in itself.
sections.repair_procedure: 1. Confirm the structural repair is signed off and that the area is dry. 2. Mask every bonding land, every fastener that must remain unprimed and any adjacent sealant fillet. 3. Prepare the surface in accordance with the applicable maintenance task, and pass the water break test. 4. Apply the sol-gel preparation within the time limit. 5. Apply the chromate-free epoxy primer to the dry film thickness given in the limits table, in two coats, allowing the flash-off time between them. 6. Feather the boundary into the surrounding scheme over not less than twenty-five millimetres. 7. Where a splice plate D5120114264366 or a stiffener DUD740691-36 is part of the repair, prime the faying edges before the topcoat. 8. Apply the topcoat. 9. Remove the masking before the topcoat is fully cured. 10. Where the swaged collar LN40979-37 is present, confirm that no primer bridges the collar to the plate. 11. Apply the sealant fillet at the repair edge after the topcoat has cured. 12. Record the dry film thickness at five points.
sections.inspection_requirements: Measure the dry film thickness at five points across the repair and record all five; a single average reading hides a thin spot at the edge, which is where the corrosion starts. Do a visual inspection of the whole boundary for a butted rather than feathered edge. Measure the bonding resistance at every land inside the repair area and compare it against the pre-repair record. Repeat the visual inspection at the next scheduled structural check and record whether any filiform corrosion has started at the boundary.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Applicable over a completed repair of any size within the lower shell, provided the structural repair itself is inside its own limits and the protective boundary does not cross a bonded joint.

repair_drawings.title: Protective scheme boundary and bonding land exclusions, lower shell

type_data.fastener_pattern: Not applicable; the scheme is applied over an existing fastener pattern and the heads are primed with the surface
type_data.fatigue_life_note: The scheme carries no load and does not affect the fatigue life of the repair beneath it. It does affect the corrosion life, and a thin boundary will start filiform corrosion within two years in a humid environment.
